message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the most recent common ancestor of the two orders **Carnivora** (the lion’s order) and **Perissodactyla** (the zebra’s order).  
Both orders belong to the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**, so the common ancestor would have been a small, insect‑eating mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago during the late Cretaceous/early Paleogene. This ancestor is far older than the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (which dates back ~100–120 million years) but is the most recent point at which the lineages leading to lions and zebras diverged.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. The common ancestor of lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) would be a common ancestor in the mammalian lineage. Both are mammals, but lions are felids (family Felidae), zebras are equids (family Equidae). They diverged from a common ancestor in the order Carnivora vs Perissodactyla? Actually lions are in order Carnivora, suborder Feliformia. Zebras are in order Perissodactyla (odd-toed ungulates). So their common ancestor would be a more distant mammalian ancestor, perhaps a placental mammal ancestor. The last common ancestor of all placental mammals is the eutherian ancestor. But maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species: that would be the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That would be the last common ancestor of the superorders Laurasiatheria? Actually Carnivora and Perissodactyla are both part of Laurasiatheria. So the last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla would be the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria. That ancestor would be a mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago. So the answer: the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is a mammal from the Laurasiatheria clade, likely a small, insectivorous mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago. Or we can say the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which is older (~100-120 million years ago). But the more precise answer: the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is a member of Laurasiatheria. So we can mention that the last common ancestor of lion and zebra was a small, insectivorous mammal that lived in the late Cretaceous or early Paleogene. Alternatively, we can say the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the superorders Laurasiatheria, which existed around 70-80 million years ago.

We should provide a concise answer. No tool needed.
